Microsoft Bob, 1995

A Windows shell that showed programs as objects in the rooms of a house, the extreme early case of the metaphor.

Source
Wikipedia: Microsoft Bob
Creator
Microsoft
Made
Released 10 March 1995; discontinued early 1996
Style
Skeuomorphism (precursor; agent-proposed, not yet reviewed by a person)
Moods
Domestic, playful, cartoonish
Evidence
The only image found is a 288 × 216 px non-free screenshot on Wikipedia, too small to describe. Based on Wikipedia.
Reviewed
28 September 2026
Rights
Link and metadata only. License: unverified. Rights policy

Context

Released on 10 March 1995 and discontinued in early 1996. “Microsoft Bob presented screens showing a house, with rooms that the user could visit containing familiar objects corresponding to computer applications, such as a desk with pen and paper and a checkbook. Clicking on the pen and paper would open the system’s word processor.” Wikipedia: Microsoft Bob.

Wikipedia’s skeuomorph article names Bob as the extreme case of the desktop metaphor, “representing different programs as objects in a home.” Wikipedia: Skeuomorph.

Why it belongs

Bob shows the metaphor without the later material realism. Its failure is a common warning against a metaphor that makes actions harder.
